lens: The absence of cited evidence facts renders any thesis on composite biomarker age panels speculative, highlighting a critical gap in available data for age-stratified multi-marker validation across diseases.
known_to_ignore: Age is a well-established confounding factor in biomarker studies
Multi-biomarker panels generally improve diagnostic accuracy over single markers
tensions: Plasma p-tau181 shows high AUC for AD neuropathology but only in cognitively impaired subgroups, suggesting age or disease stage interactions are unresolved
Biomarker panels for conditions like ovarian cancer achieve high sensitivity/specificity, but their integration with age remains unquantified in the evidence pool
gaps: Lack of primary data on how age as a continuous variable affects the performance of protein-based biomarker composites in AD
Underexplored cross-disease comparisons for age-adjusted biomarker panels, e.g., between neurodegenerative and oncology fields
reviewer_objections: No directly cited evidence supports any proposed thesis, making the conclusions unsubstantiated
The reliance on alpha hints without primary fact citations undermines scientific rigor and replicability
next_extractions: Quantify age-stratified AUC changes for plasma p-tau217 and NFL in preclinical vs. clinical AD cohorts
Investigate age-specific cutoffs for composite panels like CA-125 with cytokines in early-stage ovarian cancer detection
